rounds.proof_sketch: Input size is 128 (fixed). Block size is 256, so num_blocks = 1. Thread indices 0-255 exist, but only threads 0-127 have valid data (idx < size). Thread 255 writes 0.0f to shared_mem[255] (out-of-bounds in mutant). During reduction at stride=128, thread 127 reads shared_mem[255]. Since thread 255's contribution is always 0.0f regardless of input values (idx=255 >= size=128), the out-of-bounds access reads the 0.0f that was written, producing identical results.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation reduces shared memory from 256 to 255 elements, creating out-of-bounds access at index 255. However, with input size fixed at 128 and block size 256, thread 255 always has idx >= size, so thread_loss = 0.0f unconditionally. The out-of-bounds write stores 0.0f, and the subsequent out-of-bounds read by thread 127 (accessing shared_mem[127+128]=shared_mem[255]) retrieves this same 0.0f. Since the value is always zero regardless of input tensor contents, no value manipulation can change the corrupted location's contribution. The undefined behavior consistently produces correct results for this specific configuration.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable through value manipulation. Thread 255's contribution is always 0.0f because idx=255 >= size=128 (fixed). The out-of-bounds memory location always contains 0.0f, making the undefined behavior produce identical results. Would require changing input size to exceed 255 elements to make thread 255 process valid data, but shapes are fixed.
